newsitem.title: UK: BT unfazed by watchdog's network charge plan.
newsitem.headline: BT unfazed by watchdog's network charge plan.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Tuesday that the toughest end of a range of suggested price controls for its network charges would be "very harsh" -- but added that it was not alarmed at proposals published by the industry watchdog.

Don Cruickshank, the industry regulator who heads the Oftel watchdog body, earlier published a consultative document covering the price that BT charges other UK network operators for interconnecting with, and carrying calls over, its network.
Cruickshank suggested a price cap regime of 6-12 percent below the rate of retail price inflation (RPI-6 to RPI-12) running from October 1997 to September 2001.
But BT said a price formula of RPI-12 for this part of its business, which represents about one billion stg out of BT's total costs of 12 billion stg, could harm infrastructure investment in Britain.
"Interconnect rates in the UK are already the lowest in the world," a BT spokesman told Reuters. "It is also well known that Oftel are keen to encourage investment in infrastructure in the UK.
"The higher that the upper minus figure is, the less incentive there will be for others to invest. It is not just for us -- it is for the development of UK infrastructure," he added.
"If you're looking at a range of 6-12, 12 would be very harsh and six would be much more what we were thinking of."

The basic framework for the new controls was set out last December and overall, the proposals are expected to give BT more flexibility to set charges and mark a reduction in detailed and intrusive regulation.
BT says the framework for this kind of regulation is "very sensible", adding that it will use the consultative period, which runs until June 10, to argue for a lower price cap.
"We will be actively arguing in our normal cogent and persuasive way that it (price controls) should be lower rather than higher," the spokesman added.
Oftel's final proposals will be published in early July and if BT agrees to them, they will take effect on October 1, 1997.
